readings.title: Guardians of the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Testing the Heart
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 13:1] When there arises among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and he shall give you a sign or a wonder, [2] and the sign or the wonder shall come true, of which he spoke to you, saying, ‘Let us go after other mighty ones – which you have not known – and serve them,’ [3] do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is testing <dn>את</dn> you to know whether you love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with all your heart and with all your being. [4] Walk after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn>, and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands and obey <dn>His</dn> voice, and serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> and cling to <dn>Him</dn>. [5] And that prophet or that dreamer of dreams is put to death, because he has spoken apostasy against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> – who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim and redeemed you from the house of bondage – to thrust you out of the way in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded you to walk. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [6] When your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own being, entices you secretly, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other mighty ones,’ which you have not known, neither you nor your fathers, [7] of the mighty ones of the people which are all around you, near to you or far off from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth, [8] do not agree with him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pardon him, nor show compassion, nor conceal him, [9] but you shall certainly kill him. Your hand is first against him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people. [10] And you shall stone him with stones until he dies, because he sought to thrust you away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage. [11] And let all Yisra’ĕl hear and fear, and not again do any such evil matter as this in your midst. [12] When you hear it said in one of your cities, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you to dwell in, [13] ‘Certain men, sons of Beliya’al, have gone out from your midst and led <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other mighty ones,” which you have not known,’ [14] then you shall inquire, and search out, and ask diligently. And see, if the matter is true and established that this abomination has been done in your midst, [15] you shall certainly smite <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, putting <dn>את</dn> it under the ban, and <dn>את</dn> all that is in it and <dn>את</dn> its livestock, with the edge of the sword. [16] And gather <dn>את</dn> all its spoil into the middle of its street, and burn <dn>את</dn> the city and <dn>את</dn> all its spoil completely with fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And it shall be a heap forever, never to be built again. [17] And none of that which is put under the ban shall cling to your hand, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turns from the fierceness of <dn>His</dn> displeasure and shall show you compassion, and have compassion on you and increase you, as <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, [18] when you obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today, to do <dn>את</dn> what is right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: A Set-Apart People
readings.subtitle: Dietary Boundaries
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 14:1] You are the children of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cut yourselves nor shave the front of your head for the dead, [2] for you are a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has chosen you to be a people for <dn>Himself</dn>, a treasured possession above all the peoples who are on the face of the earth. [3] Do not eat whatever is abominable. [4] These are the beasts which you do eat: ox, sheep, and goat, [5] deer, and gazelle, and roebuck, and wild goat, and addax, and antelope, and mountain sheep. [6] And every beast that has a split hoof and completely divided into two hooves, chewing the cud among the beasts, you do eat. [7] Only, <dn>את</dn> these you do not eat among those that chew the cud or those that have a split hoof: <dn>את</dn> the camel, and <dn>את</dn> the hare, and <dn>את</dn> the rock badger, for they chew the cud but do not have a split hoof; they are unclean for you. [8] And <dn>את</dn> the pig, for it has a split hoof but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you. Do not eat their flesh nor touch their dead carcasses. [9] <dn>את</dn> These you do eat of all that are in the waters: any that has fins and scales you do eat. [10] And whatever does not have fins and scales you do not eat, it is unclean for you. [11] Eat all clean birds. [12] But these you do not eat: <dn>את</dn> the eagle, and <dn>את</dn> the vulture, and <dn>את</dn> the black vulture, [13] and <dn>את</dn> the red kite, and <dn>את</dn> the falcon, and the buzzard after its kind, [14] and <dn>את</dn> every raven after its kind, [15] and <dn>את</dn> the ostrich, and <dn>את</dn> the nighthawk, and <dn>את</dn> the seagull, and <dn>את</dn> the hawk after its kind, [16] <dn>את</dn> the little owl, and <dn>את</dn> the great owl, and <dn>את</dn> the white owl, [17] and <dn>את</dn> the pelican, and <dn>את</dn> the carrion vulture, and <dn>את</dn> the fisher owl, [18] and <dn>את</dn> the stork, and <dn>את</dn> the heron after its kind, and <dn>את</dn> the hoopoe, and <dn>את</dn> the bat. [19] And every flying insect is unclean for you, they are not eaten. [20] Eat all clean birds. [21] Do not eat any carcass. Give it to the stranger who is within your gates, that he may eat it, or sell it to a foreigner. For you are a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.

readings.title: The Consecrated Increase
readings.subtitle: The Annual and Third-Year Tithe
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 14:22] You shall tithe without fail <dn>את</dn> all the yield of your grain that the field brings forth year by year. [23] And you shall eat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, in the place where <dn>He</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell, <dn>את</dn> the tithe of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and of the firstlings of your herd and your sheep, so that you learn to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> always. [24] And when the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to bring the tithe, or when the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to set <dn>His</dn> Name is too far from you, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you, [25] then you shall give it in silver, and shall bind the silver in your hand and go to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses. [26] And you shall spend that silver for whatever your being desires: for cattle or sheep, for wine or strong drink, for whatever your being desires. And you shall eat there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall rejoice, you and your household. [27] And do not forsake the Lĕwite who is within your gates, for he has no portion nor inheritance with you. [28] At the end of every third year you shall bring out <dn>את</dn> all the tithe of your increase of that year and store it up within your gates. [29] And the Lĕwite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you in all the work of your hand which you do.

readings.title: The Economic Heart of the Kingdom
readings.subtitle: The Year of Release
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 15:1] At the end of every seven years you shall make a release. [2] And this is the matter of the release: Every holder of a loan shall release <dn>את</dn> what he has loaned to his neighbour. He does not exact it of his neighbour or his brother, because it is called the release of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] Of a foreigner you may exact it, but your hand shall release whatever is yours with your brother. [4] Only, there should be no poor among you, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly bless you in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you for an inheritance to possess, [5] only if you diligently obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all these commands which I command you today. [6] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bless you as <dn>He</dn> promised you. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. And you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you. [7] When there is a poor man with you, one of your brothers, within any of the gates in your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, do not harden <dn>את</dn> your heart nor close <dn>את</dn> your hand from your poor brother, [8] but you shall freely open <dn>את</dn> your hand to him and freely lend him enough for his need, in whatever he lacks. [9] Be on your guard lest there be a thought in your heart of Beliya’al, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near,’ and your eye be evil against your poor brother and you give him naught. And he shall cry out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against you, and it shall be sin in you. [10] You shall freely give to him, and let your heart not be grieved when you give to him, because for this reason <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does bless you in all your works and in all to which you put your hand. [11] For the poor shall never cease from the land. Therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘You shall freely open <dn>את</dn> your hand to your brother, to your poor and to your needy, in your land.’

readings.title: Freedom and Provision
readings.subtitle: The Law of the Hebrew Servant
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 15:12] When your brother, a Heḇrew man or a Heḇrew woman, is sold to you and has served you six years, then in the seventh year you shall let him go free from you. [13] And when you let him go free from you, do not let him go empty-handed. [14] You shall richly supply him from your flock, and from your threshing-floor, and from your winepress. With that which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed you, you shall give to him. [15] And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> redeemed you. Therefore I am commanding you <dn>את</dn> this matter today. [16] And it shall be, when he says to you, ‘I do not go away from you,’ because he loves you and <dn>את</dn> your house, because it is well with him with you, [17] then you shall take <dn>את</dn> an awl and thrust it through his ear to the door, and he shall be your servant forever. And do the same to your female servant. [18] Let it not be hard in your eyes when you send <dn>את</dn> him away free from you, for he has been worth a double hired servant in serving you six years. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bless you in all that you do.

readings.title: Firstfruits of the Flock
readings.subtitle: Consecrating the Firstlings
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 15:19] All the firstling males that are born of your herd and of your flock you shall set apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do no work with the firstling of your herd, nor shear the firstling of your flock. [20] You and your household shall eat it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> year by year in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses. [21] But when there is any defect in it, if it is lame or blind or has any evil defect, do not slaughter it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [22] Eat it within your gates – the unclean and the clean alike, as the gazelle and as the deer. [23] Only, do not eat <dn>את</dn> its blood, pour it on the ground like water.

readings.title: The Cycle of Remembrance
readings.subtitle: Pesah and Unleavened Bread
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 16:1] Guard <dn>את</dn> the month of Aḇiḇ, and perform the Pesaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, for in the month of Aḇiḇ <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brought you out of Mitsrayim by night. [2] And you shall slaughter the Pesaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, from the flock and the herd, in the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell. [3] Eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you eat unleavened bread with it, bread of affliction, because you came out of the land of Mitsrayim in haste – so that you remember <dn>את</dn> the day in which you came out of the land of Mitsrayim all the days of your life. [4] And no leaven should be seen with you in all your border for seven days, neither should any of the meat which you slaughter in the evening on the first day remain all night until morning. [5] You are not allowed to slaughter <dn>את</dn> the Pesaḥ within any of your gates which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you, [6] but at the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell, there you slaughter <dn>את</dn> the Pesaḥ in the evening, at the going down of the sun, at the appointed time you came out of Mitsrayim. [7] And you shall roast and eat it in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents. [8] Six days you eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a closing festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. You do no work.

readings.title: The Harvest of Weeks
readings.subtitle: Shabuoth
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 16:9] Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin to count seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the grain. [10] And you shall perform the Festival of Weeks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with a voluntary offering from your hand, which you give as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you. [11] And you shall rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lĕwite who is within your gates, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are in your midst, at the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell. [12] And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim, and you shall guard and do <dn>את</dn> these laws.

readings.title: The Gathering of the Nations
readings.subtitle: Sukkoth
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 16:13] Perform the Festival of Booths for seven days after you have gathered in from your threshing-floor and from your winepress. [14] And you shall rejoice in your festival, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lĕwite and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates. [15] Seven days you shall celebrate to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be only rejoicing. [16] Three times a year all your males appear before <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>He</dn> chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. And no one should appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> empty-handed. [17] Each one with the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> which <dn>He</dn> has given you.
